initialRequiredFindings.problem: Owners are sampled when `sampledCalls++ % 1000 == 0`, which picks calls 0, 1000, 2000, 3000 and 4000. `RepeatCallersAsync` (FlushStressFixture.cs:116) cancels the even-indexed calls and lets the odd ones time out. So all five weak samples in every repeat mode come from caller-cancelled waits. No sample comes from the 7,500 timed-out waits. Those are the waits that run the real expiry `Tick` → `observe()` → `lifetime.Cancel()` path, and they all link to the long-lived `sharedCaller.Token` (FlushStressFixture.cs:117). The doc (flush-stress-qualification.md:20) puts '7,500 cancellations and 7,500 timeouts' next to 'Five sampled deadline owners per scenario become unreachable', which implies both outcome classes were sampled. Also, nothing checks whether `sharedCaller` keeps registrations after 2,500 linked-token disposals.
initialRequiredFindings.suggestedFix: Sample both parities, for example `sampledCalls++ % 1000 is 0 or 1`. Then require 10 samples (5 cancelled, 5 timed out) all collected, in the fixture, FlushStressExpectations.cs:33 and verify-flush-stress.py:71. Optionally also report and assert the registration count on `sharedCaller` after the loop. Update the doc sentence to say which outcomes were sampled.

initialRequiredFindings.problem: The doc says 'CoreLogRuntime uses the concrete console/file writers to prepare bounded output bytes before admission. The worker invokes those same writers for sequential WriteAsync and FlushAsync operations.' Every T04 mode builds through `CoreLogRuntime.CreateQueued` (FlushStressFixture.cs:31-32) using the fixture `Writer.WriteAsync`/`FlushAsync` delegates. That leaves `consoleWriter` and `fileWriter` null, so `Prepare` never runs (CoreLogRuntime.cs:288-314). The worker writes `item.Event.JsonLine` into a MemoryStream. Line 26 of the same doc says correctly that controlled writers do this, so line 5 contradicts it and overstates what T04 qualifies. It also gives no T04 basis for the 'physical file ownership' wording.
initialRequiredFindings.suggestedFix: Rewrite paragraph 5 to say: T04 composes actual Core queues/workers/flush coordination through the internal `CreateQueued` seam with controlled in-memory writers; concrete `ConsoleOutputWriter`/`FileOutputWriter` preparation and physical file visibility/ownership are covered by earlier lanes, not by these scenarios.

resolutions.resolution: Sample both even cancellation and odd timeout paths at each 1000-call checkpoint; require all ten actual owners collected while the long-lived timeout caller token remains alive. This is an owner retention probe, not an exhaustive private CTS registration count claim.
Separate actual controlled MemoryStream stress callbacks from concrete production preparation; physical runtime/ownership evidence is bound to current supplementary result/boundary regression lanes.
All 32 actual expired callbacks must remain before linked notification/disposal after a brief guard interval and before releasing cancellation or I/O; report and exact-reason native corruption added.
Live and native assertions check both outputs retain all four/one controls after 48 callers detach; an exact-reason file-control corruption is added.

cisGraph.limitations: Extraction/compiler warnings and missing explicit verified-by edges retained; actual unit/process/native reports establish execution.

limitations: C# private Task storage/weak-owner/reflection probes are pinned .NET 10.0.12 development qualification, not public/future-language memory-layout promises.
Near-exhaustion logical counters are seeded; one physical record is distinguished from prior history.
Controlled clocks exercise UTC/elapsed semantics without changing the OS clock; managed timer resolution may overshoot tiny budgets.
Controlled MemoryStream stress is supplemented by current-assembly physical file regression; it is not an OS/filesystem latency benchmark.
Userspace flush does not imply fsync, crash durability or collector acknowledgement.
Native Ubuntu runtime execution does not qualify an absent Linux SDK/full-release lane.
Public Create/Stop/Dispose/provider, idle file scheduling in S09 and release remain later roadmap tasks.
